question: At all levels of education in Greece, there is inadequate provision for heating in winter and cooling in summer. This situation puts a strain on the educational process and is discouraging for the future citizens of our country. In winter, throughout the country and especially in regions of Northern Greece, temperatures drop excessively, with schools being forced to operate without heating.

On the other hand, towards summer, there is no cooling provided for schoolrooms. Unfortunately, in the latest Panhellenic examinations, many students were forced to write in intolerable conditions, and quite a few students brought fans with them from home. Improved air conditioning of Greek school premises can be achieved much more effectively if implemented on a large scale.

An intervention to deal with high temperatures can be achieved at basic level by adding tents and trees for shade, and also (at least) ceiling fans for cooling. For heating, heat pumps can be used, as well as solar panels on school roofs, together with the existing structures. In all cases, the addition of suitable door and window frames would be necessary. In view of this: 1.
Under which programmes is funding available for improved air-conditioning in school buildings?
What are the amounts available for Greece for the current programming period?
Could at least the municipalities with responsibility for operating schools have access to interest-free funding for such investments?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.9.2024) 1. For the programming period 2021-2027, with the support of the EU Cohesion Funds, the 13 regional programmes as well as the sectoral programme ‘Environment and Climate Change’ have earmarked funding to support Greece in improving energy efficiency for public buildings, including schools.

Under the programme for the environment and climate action ‘LIFE’, and its sub-programme ‘clean energy transition’ (CET), funding can be awarded to projects supporting the climate neutrality of heating and cooling. The focus is hereby on ‘new solutions and business models’1. 2. The total amount available under the Cohesion Policy concerning this type of actions is EUR 461.7 million (public expenditure).

Under LIFE, the total available budget at the EU level under the CET sub-programme is EUR 997 million. No specific amount is reserved for Greece, as eligible proposals from all countries compete for funding. 3. Cohesion funding falls under the principle of shared management, therefore, the Member State is fully responsible for the project selection and implementation of the programmes.
It should be noted that operational costs of projects are not eligible for EU co-financing. LIFE is implemented through grants with maximum EU co-financing rates of 95%.
1 Further information and currently open calls: https://cinea.ec.europa.eu/programmes/life_en
